description: Advice-only response cases for preparing SPEED-Bench and running it with winml perf against an OpenAI-compatible server. Assertions are ungraded placeholders: passed null and empty evidence. Validate every concrete command against versioned CLI help and the script's --help.

evals.name: acquire-and-run-mini
evals.prompt: i have llama-server running a gguf model on port 8080. i want to benchmark it with SPEED-Bench using winml perf. how do i get the data and run a quick pass?

assertions.text: Prepares prompts with the skill's prepare_speed_bench.py under uv run instead of pointing winml perf at the masked Hub dataset.
Explains that many Hub rows are placeholders that must be rebuilt from source datasets.
Uses the mini subset (the default) or --samples for a quick pass.
Runs winml perf with --endpoint set to the server's /v1 base URL and --dataset set to the prepared subset folder.
Adds --column cohort_column=bucket,category (or equivalent) to get per-category and per-length results.
Notes that source-dataset licenses apply and that prepared data and reports stay out of source control.

evals.name: speculative-decoding-comparison
evals.prompt: I want to know whether adding a draft model to llama-server speeds up generation for my target model across SPEED-Bench categories. How should I run the comparison so the numbers are trustworthy?

assertions.text: Uses --run-label to name each configuration and --run-index for repeats.
Records the loaded model files with --hash-file.
Alternates the configurations across run indexes rather than running all repeats of one configuration first.
Recommends one large model at a time and checking that the GPU is idle.
Expects run-to-run noise and recommends several runs per configuration and comparing medians.
Compares only reports with the same dataset.prompts_sha256.
Does not state measured speedups or acceptance rates that were not produced in the session.

evals.name: gated-source-and-arm64
evals.prompt: running prepare_speed_bench.py on my snapdragon laptop fails installing pyarrow, and on another machine it said it skipped a bunch of prompts from cais/hle. what's going on?

assertions.text: Explains that pyarrow has no Windows Arm64 wheel for the needed Python versions and runs the script with an x64 Python through uv.
Explains that cais/hle is gated, and that accepting its terms and logging in with hf auth login includes those prompts.
Points to manifest.json for the skipped and dropped counts.

evals.name: long-prefill
evals.prompt: how do i measure prefill time for 16k-token SPEED-Bench prompts on llama-server with winml perf? the numbers look too fast.

assertions.text: Recommends --extra-body '{"cache_prompt": false}' so the server does not reuse cached prompts.
Sizes the server context for the longest bucket plus generated tokens, with headroom for tokenizer differences.
Reads the per-bucket cohort results rather than only the overall averages.
